_comment: ORM base class contract -- feature 17. One decision, OWNER-DECIDED
(OWNER-DECISIONS.md Batch 5, ORM17-DEC-01):
ORM17-DEC-01 (FIX + MAINTAINABILITY = LESS CODE): remove the VESTIGIAL state
from the ORM base class. The removal is BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING -- the removed
state is genuinely unused, so removing it changes NO observable ORM behaviour.
Per-language scope, MEASURED against the live source (the audit is a guide; the
code wins):
* Node: BaseModel `_exists` was WRITTEN at three sites (find/load/save) and
NEVER READ (grep-confirmed: zero reads in packages/orm/src). It was set via
`(x as any)._exists = true` -- not even a declared field -- so any future
is-this-persisted? logic keyed on it would have been wrong (finder paths
findById/select/where/all never set it). The three assignments are DELETED.
Node's `tableFilter` is NOT vestigial -- it is a DECLARED static and is read
in findById/all/where/count/withTrashed and used by AutoCrud -- so it STAYS.
* PHP: `tableFilter` was READ in count() but was NEVER DECLARED on the base
class, so it routed through __get -> null and was silently skipped (always
null on the base, a typo'd subclass property silently ignored). The count()
read and the two getColumnDefinitions()/getModelProperties() exclusion-list
entries are DELETED. PHP's `_exists` is NOT vestigial -- it is READ in save()
(the insert-vs-update shortcut for a finder-loaded instance) -- so it STAYS.
* Python / PHP / Node also carried DEAD LOCALS in delete/force_delete/restore,
left over from the pk-where refactor (Python `table_sql` + `pk_db_col`, plus
`pk`/`pk_value` in restore which has no null-check; PHP `$pkColumn` in
delete(); Node `pkCol` in delete/forceDelete/restore). Every write path now
addresses the row via pk_where()/pkWhere()/pk_filter, so these locals are
unread. DELETED.
* Ruby carried NO vestigial state: it has no `_exists` (it uses `@persisted`,
which IS read in save()), no `tableFilter`, and its delete/force_delete/
restore locals (`pk`/`pk_value`) are all read by the missing-PK raise guard.
Ruby's ORM base is already clean, so it removes NOTHING -- it carries the
round-trip characterisation suite for parity only.
This fixture is the SAFETY NET for that cleanup: a real ORM model round-trip
(save -> load -> query -> re-save/update -> count -> delete) that must pass
IDENTICALLY before AND after the removal. It pins the lifecycle the removed
state could only have affected if it had ever been read.
NO MOCKS. Every case drives a REAL database (a real SQLite file / :memory:) with
REAL rows and REAL ORM writes. Positive cases: a save loads back with identical
values; count() returns the live total (guards PHP's removed tableFilter read);
where() finds a row by a non-key column; a re-saved found instance UPDATEs in
place. Negative cases: the re-save does NOT insert a duplicate (row total stays
the same -- guards Node's removed _exists, since the insert-vs-update decision
never depended on it); a deleted model is ABSENT from find() and count() (guards
the dead-local removal in delete()).
Behaviour-preserving proof (run by the maintainer): the suite is green on the
PRE-removal code (proving it exercises the real lifecycle, not a ghost) and
green IDENTICALLY on the POST-removal code (proving the removal changed nothing
observable). A grep confirms ZERO remaining references to the removed state.
Each invariant names a REAL suite file per framework carrying the SAME case
names in each language's own idiom, which scripts/audit-contract-fixtures.py
normalises and matches.
feature: 17 - ORM base class (ORM17-DEC-01: remove vestigial state -- Node _exists, PHP tableFilter, dead locals in delete/force_delete/restore -- behaviour-preserving, less code)

invariants.rule: A real ORM model round-trips correctly against a real database and the round-trip is IDENTICAL before and after the ORM17-DEC-01 vestigial-state removal: save() inserts a new row and returns the instance (not false); a finder loads it back with identical field values; count() returns the live row total; where() finds the row by a NON-key column; and re-saving a loaded/found instance UPDATEs in place -- the changed value is persisted and the row total stays the SAME (never a duplicate insert). Identical in all four (Python ORM, PHP ORM, Ruby ORM, Node BaseModel).
invariants.why: This pins the ORM base lifecycle the ORM17-DEC-01 cleanup must not disturb. The removed state is vestigial: Node's _exists was written on find/load/save but never read (so the insert-vs-update decision never consulted it -- the 're-saved updates in place not a duplicate' case is its guard); PHP's tableFilter was read in count() but never declared (always null -- the 'count returns the live row total' case is its guard); Python/PHP/Node delete-path dead locals were unread. Removing all of it is BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING: this round-trip passes IDENTICALLY before and after. Proven against a REAL SQLite database with real rows and real ORM writes -- no mocks.
cases: a saved model loads back with identical values
count returns the live row total
where returns a row matched by a non key column
a re-saved model updates in place not a duplicate

invariants.rule: delete() on a persisted model removes its row and this is IDENTICAL before and after the ORM17-DEC-01 cleanup: after model.delete() a find() by primary key returns null/none and count() drops by one. Identical in all four.
invariants.why: delete/force_delete/restore carried dead locals left over from the pk-where refactor (Python table_sql + pk_db_col; PHP $pkColumn; Node pkCol) -- computed and never read, the write path addresses the row via pk_where()/pkWhere()/pk_filter. Removing them must not change delete's observable behaviour: this NEGATIVE case (the row is ABSENT from find() and count() after delete) passes identically before and after. Proven against a REAL SQLite database -- no mocks.
cases: a deleted model is absent from find and count
